content.text:
I reviewed all 8 units. Only one possible defect came up, and it depends on code that isn't shown. Two units need a human look:

- **`compactHeadViewLocked`**: whether it loses data rests entirely on how `committedAppendID()` (not shown) works. The new comment says samples with an appendID at or below the watermark are "guaranteed to be present in some generated block". That only holds if `committedAppendID()` returns the highest ID below which *every* appender has finished. If it returns the highest ID any appender has committed, an older appender that commits late can be evicted and its sample lost on WAL replay. The new test opens only one late appender, so it can't tell the two apart.
- **`filterSeriesAndSortPostings`**: for the stale case it matches the old code. With a nil `keep` it now reads series without taking the lock, and what it filters out is checked again at eviction.

The other six units are a benchmark, a test hook, and renames, so a skim or nothing is enough.

units.summary: Pulls the old stale-compaction loop into a shared helper for both stale and selected-series compaction. Changes: it captures an appendID watermark before writing blocks, skips the reload and log when a chunk-range slice produced no block, calls the test hook, and passes the watermark to the evictor. Whether eviction can lose data depends on how committedAppendID is defined.

issues.title: Watermark guarantee depends on committedAppendID being a low watermark
issues.evidence:
appendIDWatermark := db.head.iso.committedAppendID()
// Samples with appendID <= watermark are guaranteed to be present in some
issues.failure_scenario: Appender A opens and gets ID 5. Appender B opens with ID 6 and commits. Compaction starts. If committedAppendID returns 6 (highest committed ID) rather than 4 (highest ID below which all are complete), A commits during the write/evict window. A's sample has ID 5, which is not above the watermark, so the series is evicted and the sample is lost after WAL replay.

units.headline: Shared head-view compaction helper with appendID eviction watermark
units.reason: New eviction-safety logic on a persistence path where data can be lost.
focus: committedAppendID returns the highest ID such that all IDs at or below it have finished, not the highest committed ID
The isolation-disabled path: watermark 0 means no protection against concurrent writes
A reloadBlocks failure on a later slice leaves earlier blocks persisted but no series evicted
mint is computed with opts.ChunkRange but stepped with chunkRange.Load() (inherited from the old code)
